summary: The study investigates the effect of S-termination on a Ge(1 0 0) surface prior to ALD HfO2 deposition. The ALD process was performed at 350 8C using water vapor and Hf[N(C2H5)CH3]4 as precursors. The interfacial GeOS layer thickness was found to be thinner on the S-terminated surface compared to the O3-oxidized surface, leading to a lower equivalent oxide thickness (EOT) and improved leakage current characteristics.
evidence: The ALD process for depositing HfO2 was performed using water vapor and Hf[N(C2H5)CH3]4 (tetrakisethylmethylaminohafnium, TEMAH) on the S-terminated Ge surface. It was found that the oxidized surface had a GeO2 structure. The processing times for water vapor and Hf[N(C2H5)CH3]4 were 0.5 and 2 s, respectively. A 35-s N2 purge was performed after the introduction of each precursor. In order to target 4 and 8 nm of HfO2, 44 and 88 ALD cycles were conducted at 350 8C.
